en: The Philippine archipelago contains 7,641 islands, making it one of the largest archipelagic countries in the world by total island count.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape, rising 2,462 meters high with slopes averaging 35 degrees.
The Cagayan River in Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers in Luzon.
The critically endangered tamaraw, found only on Mindoro island, has a wild population of fewer than 500 individuals left today.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an 8.2-kilometer underground navigable waterway, making it one of the longest in the world.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones each year, with most of these storms entering through the eastern Pacific region.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects a 96,828-hectare marine sanctuary containing over 600 distinct fish species.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering approximately 14,649 square kilometers of islands and waters.
The Philippine Rise, an underwater plateau east of Luzon, spans an expansive area of 13 million hectares beneath the Pacific Ocean.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches about 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon, acting as a massive natural typhoon barrier.
